name: wimlib
desc: Library to create, extract, and modify Windows Imaging files
why: Opens Windows Imaging files up for inspection and modification, a decent look inside a closed file format.

brief.what_it_is: wimlib is an open source, cross-platform C library for creating, extracting, and modifying Windows Imaging (WIM) archives. Its command-line frontend, wimlib-imagex, is the tool most people will use, and the brew package installs it as many separate wim* executables such as wimapply, wimcapture, wimdir, wiminfo, and wimverify. WIM files go in and extracted files, directory listings, or new or modified WIM archives come out. It also handles ESD (.esd) archives, which are WIM archives that use solid LZMS compression.
brief.why_it_exists: WIM is a Windows archive format that is somewhat like ZIP but also stores Windows-specific metadata, holds multiple images in one file, and deduplicates content. wimlib is pitched as a free, cross-platform alternative to Microsoft's WIMGAPI, ImageX, and DISM, so non-Windows systems can read and write these files.
brief.how_it_works: Each distinct file content is identified by its SHA-1 digest and stored only once per archive, even when it is referenced by several images, duplicate files, hard links, or named data streams. wimlib performs this deduplication automatically when creating or updating an archive. It implements XPRESS, LZX, and LZMS compression, with LZX as the default, and can use solid mode. On Windows it uses native API calls to handle NTFS features; on UNIX it handles hard and symbolic links and can optionally store uids, gids, modes, and extended attributes.

commands_seen.context: Clones the official source repository from wimlib.net, which the homepage gives for developers.
Clones the GitHub mirror of the same source repository.

brief.install_notes: Downloads are a source tarball for UNIX and Linux, plus 32-bit and 64-bit Windows binaries and an experimental Windows ARM64 build. Windows binaries are said to cover Windows XP and later. The homepage gives no other installation steps, accounts, or configuration.
brief.standout: The homepage stresses that wimlib writes NTFS-correct archives (ACLs, attributes, links, named streams) and can deploy Windows from Linux, including capturing NTFS block devices through NTFS-3G. It also says its LZX and LZMS compressors typically beat Microsoft's own implementations, and offers them as standalone libraries for other formats.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists wimlib-1.14.5 as the current release, dated January 29, 2026. Copyright runs through 2026 and the source is on git and GitHub with pull requests accepted.
brief.caveats: Mounting a WIM (wimmount, wimmountrw) is Linux-only and relies on FUSE. wimlib cannot decrypt Microsoft's partially encrypted ESD archives. The Windows ARM64 build is marked EXPERIMENTAL. Block-device capture and apply depend on NTFS-3G on UNIX. The homepage does not list a license beyond saying a COPYING file ships with the software.
quotes: wimlib is an open source, cross-platform library for creating, extracting, and modifying Windows Imaging (WIM) archives.
Provides independent, high quality open source compressors and decompressors for several compression formats used by Microsoft which are not as well known as more open formats.
Contributions are accepted via GitHub pull request or any other convenient means.
